findings.title: Escaped action keys evade pin checks
findings.description: `USES_ANYWHERE` matches only literal `uses`, so `unpinnedUses` skips a YAML key such as `"\u0075ses": actions/checkout@v5` before either the unsupported-form or SHA check runs. YAML resolves that quoted key to `uses`, allowing a workflow step to use a moving-tag action while `workflowPinProblems` reports no problem and the required check passes.

evidence.explanation: The new guard requires the literal characters `uses` followed by a colon; an escaped quoted key contains no such sequence, and the early return prevents all subsequent validation. The repository-wide test calls this scanner through `workflowPinProblems`, so it inherits the miss.

findings.title: Workflow checks reject harmless run text
findings.description: `OTHER_USES_KEY` searches for `, uses:` anywhere on a line, including inside a quoted `run` value, and `unpinnedUses` reports the line as an unsupported action. A valid step such as `- run: 'echo ", uses: not-an-action"'` therefore makes the repository-wide action-pin test fail when it appears in a workflow.

evidence.explanation: The new fallback regex has an unanchored comma branch, so it matches the comma inside the example's quoted `run` value; the unmatched-line branch then records a problem. The repository test requires every scanned workflow to have zero problems, and `npm run check` runs that test.

findings.title: An unpinned step written as `uses :` still passes
findings.description: The fallback `OTHER_USES_KEY` regex only catches an unquoted key when a `{` or `,` comes before it; a block-style key needs quotes to match, and `USES` needs `uses:` with no space before the colon. So `- uses : actions/checkout@v5`, which is valid YAML and which GitHub runs as a normal step, matches neither regex, gets dropped without a report, and `workflowPinProblems` returns no problems for a moving tag.

evidence.explanation: `USES` is `/^\s*(?:-\s+)?uses:\s*(.*)$/`, so it needs `uses:` with nothing between the key and the colon. The first branch of `OTHER_USES_KEY` only allows a quoted key (`"uses"|'uses'`). The second branch needs a `[{,]` before the key. A line like `  - uses : actions/checkout@v5` fails all three and hits the plain `return`. The new test only covers quoted keys and flow mappings (lines 61-64), not an unquoted key with a space before the colon.

findings.title: A `#` in a quoted name hides an inline step
findings.description: Before `OTHER_USES_KEY` is tested, `unpinnedUses` removes everything from the first `#` with `line.replace(/#.*$/, '')`, and it does this without checking whether the `#` sits inside a quoted string. In a step like `- {name: "Fix #12", uses: actions/checkout@v5}`, the `uses:` part is cut off before the check runs, so the step is neither reported nor checked.

evidence.explanation: Line 44 strips `#.*$` from the raw line and only then tests `OTHER_USES_KEY`. With the input `  - {name: "Fix #12", uses: actions/checkout@v5}`, the stripped text is `  - {name: "Fix `. That has no `[{,]\s*uses\s*:`, so nothing gets pushed. In YAML, a `#` only starts a comment when whitespace comes before it and it is outside quotes.

findings.title: Actions tagged without a `v` can't be pinned
findings.description: `RELEASE_COMMENT` is `/^#\s*v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`, so it only accepts a `v`-prefixed `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Releases tagged `1.2.3`, `v1.2.3-rc.1` or `v2.0.0+build` can never pass, even though the ticket asks for the 'exact release tag'. Anyone who later pins such an action has to write a tag that doesn't exist upstream (for example, add a `v` that the real tag lacks) or change the checker.

location.code_snippet:
+// The exact release the SHA was taken from, not a moving tag or a note (Qodo local review af5d2700).
+const RELEASE_COMMENT = /^#\s*v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;

evidence.explanation: The regex hard-codes a leading `v` and allows nothing after the patch number. The test at lines 72-78 even rejects `# 5.1.0`, which is the exact tag name for actions that don't use a `v` prefix. AGENTS.md and the ticket call for the exact release tag, not a `v`-prefixed one.
